purpose: svapaṭhanārtham (copied by the scribe for his own study)
notes: The two eras conflict. 'śaṃvat 18017' is corrupt. Read as VS 1817 (the catalogue's reading) it gives c. 1760 CE, but ŚS 1691 gives Nov/Dec 1769 CE. VS 1826 would match ŚS 1691, so the 0 in '18017' may be a stray digit or a miswriting of 2. The catalogue has 'ŚS 1681', which looks like the cataloguer amending the śāka toward VS 1817 (1681+135 = 1816, still off by one). The month, ayana and season agree with each other (Mārgaśīrṣa, dakṣiṇāyana, Hemanta). The father's name 'rāvalaharibhā itasya' is most likely 'Rāvala Haribhāī, tasya ātmaja'. Rāvala is a western Indian (Gujarati/Rajasthani) brahmin surname. Vāripura is unidentified; it is the father's residence and is taken as the place of copying only by inference (catalogue). 'lakṣmyaṃke' is the poem's signature word (lakṣmī-aṅka), not a person.
